title: Physics of the eye
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: X-EYE-2#t4 term and clue written for the game; X-EYE-2#t3 term and clue written for the game; X-EYE-2#t1 term and clue written for the game; X-EYE-2#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: X-EYE-2#N.3, X-EYE-2#N.5, X-EYE-2#N.7, X-EYE-2#N.8.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Range of vision
items.clue: All the object distances an eye sees clearly; a spectacle lens shifts both of its ends.

items.label: Virtual image
items.clue: What the eye actually looks at through a spectacle lens; its distance v is taken as negative.

items.label: Near point
items.clue: Closest distance at which an eye focuses: 25 cm for a normal eye, 75 cm for the long-sighted example.

items.label: Far point
items.clue: Greatest distance at which an eye focuses: infinity for a normal eye, 25 cm for the short-sighted example.

questions.stem: A long-sighted woman has a near point of 50 cm and a far point at infinity. She wears reading glasses of power +2.0 D. What is her range of vision while wearing them?
questions.explanation: Near: v = −0.50 m, 1/u = 2.0 + 2.0 = 4.0, u = 0.25 m. Far: image at infinity, so u = f = 1/2.0 = 0.50 m.

questions.stem: A short-sighted student's far point is 0.50 m from his eye. He wears old glasses of power −1.5 D. What is his far point while wearing them?
A student with normal eyesight (near point 25 cm, far point at infinity) tries on a friend's glasses of power −2.5 D. What is her range of vision through them?
questions.explanation: v = −0.25 m: 1/u = −2.5 + 4.0 = 1.5, u = 0.67 m. Distant objects give an image 0.40 m away, which she can still focus.

questions.stem: A short-sighted patient has a near point of 10 cm and a far point of 40 cm. She is given glasses of power −2.5 D. What is her range of vision while wearing them?
questions.explanation: Far: f = −0.40 m, so distant objects image at her far point. Near: v = −0.10 m, 1/u = −2.5 + 10 = 7.5, u = 0.13 m.
